'''Robert Eugene Megginson''' is an American mathematician, the Arthur F. Thurnau Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>[http://dept.math.lsa.umich.edu/people/facultyDetail.php?uniqname=meggin Faculty detail], University of Michigan mathematics, retrieved 2016-06-13.</ref> His research concerns [[functional analysis]] and [[Banach space]]s;<ref name="maa"/> he is the author of the textbook ''An Introduction to Banach Space Theory'' ([[Graduate Texts in Mathematics|GTM 183]], Springer, 1998).<ref>Review of ''An Introduction to Banach Space Theory'' by Ehrhard Behrends (1999), {{MR|1650235}}.</ref>

Megginson was born in 1948 in [[Washington, Illinois]], of [[Oglala Sioux]] heritage on his mother's side,<ref name="maa"/> and grew up in [[Sheldon, Illinois]], where his father was mayor.<ref name="interview">{{citation|url=http://www.maa.org/sites/default/files/pdf/centennial/BobMegginsonInterview.pdf|title=Interview with Bob Megginson|date=January 6, 2011|first=Kenneth A.|last=Ross|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|accessdate=2016-06-13}}.</ref> He earned a degree in physics from the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]] in 1969, and became a software specialist for the [[Roper Technologies|Roper Corporation]] until 1977, when he returned to graduate school.<ref name="maa">{{Cite web |title=Dr. Robert Eugene Megginson 1948 |url=https://nativepartnership.org/dr-robert-eugene-megginson-1948/ |access-date=2026-03-27 |website=PWNA |language=en}}</ref> He earned a master's degree in statistics in 1983,<ref name="cv">[http://www.msri.org/people/staff/meggin/Vita.pdf Curriculum vitae], retrieved 2016-06-13.</ref> He completed his Ph.D. in 1984 at the University of Illinois, with a thesis on [[normed vector space]]s supervised by [[Mahlon Marsh Day]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=4199}}</ref>
This accomplishment made him one of only approximately 12 [[Native Americans in the United States|Native Americans]] to hold a doctorate in mathematics, and he has taken great interest in underrepresented minorities in mathematics.<ref name="maa"/> 

Because his wife was employed nearby in [[Decatur, Illinois]],<ref name="interview"/> Megginson took a teaching position in 1983, joining the faculty of [[Eastern Illinois University]] as an assistant professor, rather than doing postdoctoral research. He moved to the University of Michigan in 1992, was on leave as the deputy director of the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] in [[Berkeley, California]] from 2002 to 2004, and became the Thurnau Professor at Michigan in 2008.<ref name="cv"/>

Megginson won the U.S. Presidential Award for Excellence in Science, Mathematics, and Engineering Mentoring in 1997.<ref>{{citation|last1=Robert |first1=Megginson |url=http://grantome.com/grant/NSF/DUE-9724871|title=Megginson, Robert|work=Presidential Awards for Excellence in Science, Mathematics and Engineering Mentoring|publisher=[[National Science Foundation]]|accessdate=2016-06-13}}.</ref> The [[American Indian Science and Engineering Society]] gave him their Ely S. Parker Award for lifetime service to the Native American community in 1999.<ref name="cv"/> The [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] elected him as a [[fellow]] in 2009,<ref>{{citation|url=http://ur.umich.edu/0910/Jan11_10/403-ten-university-scientists-named-aaas-fellows|title=Eleven university scientists named AAAS Fellows|magazine=University Record Online|publisher=University of Michigan|first=Laura|last=Bailey|date=January 11, 2010}}.</ref> and in the same year the [[Mathematical Association of America]] gave him their Yueh-Gin Gung and Dr. Charles Y. Hu Award for Distinguished Service, for his work on underrepresented minorities.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200905/rtx090500633p.pdf|title=MAA Prizes Presented in Washington, DC|journal=[[Notices of the AMS]]|date=May 2009|pages=633–635|volume=56|issue=5}}.</ref> In 2012, Megginson became one of the inaugural fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2016-06-13.</ref>
